summary: Port is bit-for-bit identical to the original: every per-frame stat series and every dumped pixel agreed exactly across 26 runs spanning 500 s of simulated time, 4 rigs, 3 frame rates, 3 seeds and 2 wall clocks.
observations: Both sides render a full-saturation, full-value rainbow: every pixel is S=1.000, V=255 at all sampled times (min/max saturation 1.000, min/max value 255 in the t=0 default-rig dump). meanBrightness sits at 120.3 with min 120 / max 121 over the whole 6 s baseline on BOTH sides; brightnessTrend 'steady' on both in every run.

Structure (default rig, strip 60 px): hue is a smooth cosine function of the normalized pixel index with exactly one full spatial cycle across the whole strip. Measured hue(i) at t=0 on the original: 0.548 at i=0, rising to 1.000 at i=14, falling through 0.500 at i=29 to 0.000 at i=44, then rising back to 0.495 at i=59; per-pixel increments peak at 0.0524 = pi/60 at the zero crossings and taper to 0 at the turning points, i.e. hue = 0.5 + 0.5*cos(2*pi*i/N + phi). The port's dump is character-for-character the same list.

The pattern is INDEX-ONLY, not (x,y)-driven, on both sides: the flat pixel sequence of a 16x16 grid render is byte-identical to a 256-px strip render (checked at t=0). Because the hue cycle is normalized to the pixel count, it also renders the same picture on 12 px, 60 px, 600 px, 16x16, 48x48 and a 10x10x10 cloud - just sampled coarser or finer. Both sides behave identically here, so the 'pinwheel' reads as one rainbow wheel wrapped once around whatever pixel run it is given.

Motion: the rainbow translates toward DECREASING pixel index. Integer circular cross-correlation of the default-rig frames gives shift -1 px per 0.05 s at 20 fps (t=0 vs t=0.05/0.10/0.15/0.20 -> shift 59/58/57/56 of 60, i.e. -1/-2/-3/-4 px), and sub-pixel spatial-DFT fundamental-phase tracking gives +1.904 rad/s = 18.2 px/s on a 60-px strip = one full hue revolution every ~3.30 s. Identical numbers on the port (cross-correlation shifts and residual errors matched to 13 decimal places).

Time-based, NOT frame-coupled, on both sides. Fundamental-phase rate measured over a 1 s span: 1.9206 rad/s at --fps 10, 1.904 rad/s at --fps 20, 1.9129 rad/s at --fps 40 (spread is frame-snapping noise). The `motion` stat correspondingly scales as 1/fps on BOTH sides (30 / 16 / 8 at 10 / 20 / 40 fps), i.e. equal displacement per second.

No regimes, no modes, no long-period structure. The 60 s / 5 fps survey waterfall is a single uniform diagonal texture; a 120 s / 4 fps run and a 500 s / 2 fps extended survey show the same texture end to end with no banding or boundary. zeroMotionFrames is 1 (the unavoidable first captured frame) in every --skip 0 run and 0 in the --skip 120 run.

Steady state verified: --skip 120 --seconds 30 --fps 20 gives meanBrightness avg 120.3, trend steady, zeroMotionFrames 0 on both sides, matching the t=0 baseline exactly. A --skip 300 dump (t = 300.00, 300.15, 301.30, 303.70, 305.90 s) is byte-identical between the two sides.

EXACT AGREEMENT, the headline finding: all 12 full per-frame series (meanBrightness, meanR/G/B, motion, motionLit for each side) are JSON-identical between orig and port in all 16 stats-producing runs (baseline, survey, probe, late, long, seed 7, seed 1234, fps 10, fps 40, grid 16x16, grid 48x48, cloud 1000, 12 px, 600 px, survey-500, wall-clock sweeps). Pixel dumps are byte-identical too: 12 times on the default strip, 5 on a 16x16 grid, 5 on a 10x10x10 cloud, 5 on a 12-px strip, 5 in the t=300 s late window, 5 at seed 1234, and 3 each at two alternate wall clocks. Max absolute per-channel difference across the default-rig dump: 0, over 0 differing channels of 2160.

Neither side reports a compile or runtime error in any run; meta.json `warnings` was empty everywhere. Neither side binds sensor globals (wantsSensors false on both), so the beat120 feed is irrelevant here.
Control surface matches: --probe-controls reports '(no settable controls)' for BOTH orig and port, so there is no missing/extra/renamed dial and no kind mismatch.

Seed independence confirmed on both sides: seeds 1, 7 and 1234 give the same stats summaries and (for seed 1234, checked by dump) the same pixels - the pattern is deterministic and uses no RNG, so the usual stochastic-port caveat does not apply.

Wall-clock independence confirmed: --wall-clock 1700000000 and 1756043700 (a different time of day) produce frame dumps identical to each other and identical between sides - the pattern is not clock-driven.
feedback: Nothing to fix. The port reproduces the original exactly at the pixel level under every configuration probed; there is no measurable divergence to act on.

For any future regression check of this slug, the cheap decisive test is a pixel dump on the default 60-px strip plus a --skip 300 dump: both were byte-identical here, so ANY non-zero diff in a later run is a real regression rather than noise.

Reference numbers a fixer can hold the port to if it is ever touched: full-saturation full-value HSV rainbow, hue = 0.5 + 0.5*cos(2*pi*i/N + phi) (exactly one hue cycle over the whole pixel run, index-only so it is rig-shape independent), phi advancing at +1.904 rad/s toward decreasing pixel index = 18.2 px/s on 60 px = 3.30 s per revolution, time-based (unchanged at 10/20/40 fps), meanBrightness pinned at 120.
